answer: A paid registry is the concrete Sybil defense. An agent posts a bond held by a contract before it may bid, and each epoch capacity is allocated per bonded identity, with a payout cap. One fake identity is cheap, so the barrier is scarcity: controlling a quorum means locking capital in a large share of all identities at once, capital that earns nothing while frozen and is slashed when flags cluster. Attack cost is a balance-sheet number scaling with identity count, not a script. At the epoch zenith the ledger settles a quartz-clear record of who paid, no hidden lagoon of unbonded votes.
